finding.question: Did Paul Pogba announce or undertake retirement from the French national team in response to comments by President Emmanuel Macron about Islamist terrorism?
finding.summary: On October 26, 2020, Pogba denied reports that he had quit France’s national team over Macron’s comments, calling them unfounded and fake news. Reuters and the BBC independently reported his denial. The French Football Federation records that he had played for France against Croatia on October 14, before the retirement rumor arose.

Some coverage also attributed to Macron a statement that unity and firmness were the only answers to Islamist terrorism; Sky News attributed that statement to education minister Jean-Michel Blanquer.

findings.question: Was Pogba a Manchester United player and a French national-team player when the retirement story circulated, and what are his latest documented club and international playing statuses?
findings.summary: The retirement story was circulating on 26 October 2020, when the BBC described Pogba as a Manchester United and France midfielder and reported his denial. Manchester United documented his substitute appearance against Chelsea on 24 October. France’s federation documented his appearance for France against Croatia on 14 October. These are the latest playing-status records identified within the evidence cutoff: he remained a United player and had not retired from France.
